common_name: Claudia Wannamaker Southern Magnolia (Fast-Growing Pyramidal Southern Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown or balled-and-burlapped trees in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Claudia Wannamaker is a fast-growing, densely pyramidal southern magnolia selected in South Carolina, widely planted across the Deep South.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade. Claudia Wannamaker, selected in South Carolina, bears the classic large, creamy-white, lemon-scented southern magnolia blooms on a notably fast-growing, densely pyramidal tree with glossy, deep green leaves and attractive rusty-brown leaf undersides, making it one of the most widely planted southern magnolia cultivars across the Deep South for its reliable, uniform growth habit. Water deeply during establishment, mulch to conserve moisture, and prune only to remove dead or damaged wood, since magnolias need little routine pruning.

common_name: Hasse Southern Magnolia (Narrow Columnar Fast-Growing Selection)

planting.note: Plant container-grown or balled-and-burlapped trees in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Hasse is a narrow, columnar southern magnolia that grows faster than most other narrow selections.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade. Hasse bears the classic large, creamy-white, lemon-scented southern magnolia blooms and glossy evergreen foliage on a narrow, tightly columnar form similar in shape to Alta, but noted for faster growth, filling in more quickly to provide screening or a formal vertical accent in tight side yards where a full-spreading southern magnolia would be too wide. Water deeply during establishment, mulch to conserve moisture, and prune only to remove dead or damaged wood, since magnolias need little routine pruning.

common_name: Timeless Beauty Southern Magnolia (Compact Heavy-Blooming Selection)

planting.note: Plant container-grown or balled-and-burlapped trees in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Timeless Beauty is a compact southern magnolia selection noted for especially heavy, reliable flowering at a younger age than the species.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade. Timeless Beauty bears the classic large, creamy-white, lemon-scented southern magnolia blooms in heavy abundance from a younger age than many seedling-grown trees, on a more compact, densely branched form than the largest species specimens, making it a strong choice where a full-sized magnolia's eventual scale is a concern but heavy flowering is still wanted. Water deeply during establishment, mulch to conserve moisture, and prune only to remove dead or damaged wood, since magnolias need little routine pruning.

planting.note: Plant container-grown or balled-and-burlapped trees in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Victoria is a cold-hardy southern magnolia selection with rounded, glossy leaves, originating from a hardy Canadian-grown specimen.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade. Victoria bears the classic large, creamy-white, lemon-scented southern magnolia blooms on a tree noted for exceptional cold hardiness beyond typical species range, with rounded, glossy dark-green leaves and good resistance to winter leaf burn. Its improved cold tolerance extends southern magnolia's usable range further north than most cultivars, while it performs equally well in the milder Gulf South. Water deeply during establishment, mulch to conserve moisture, and prune only to remove dead or damaged wood.
